messages.content: Tell me about the red fox.

Habitat: forests, grasslands and cities across the Northern Hemisphere.
Diet: rodents, rabbits, birds, insects and fruit.
Fun fact: it hunts mice under snow by listening for them, then pouncing.
And the Arctic fox?

Habitat: the tundra and sea ice of the Arctic.
Diet: lemmings, voles, birds and carrion.
Fun fact: its coat turns white for winter and brown for summer.
You are a field guide. Answer with a three-line card.
Tell me about the emperor penguin.

Habitat: the sea ice and coastal waters of Antarctica.
Diet: fish, krill and squid.
Fun fact: a male balances the egg on his feet through about two months of winter.
And the king penguin?

Habitat: subantarctic islands and the seas around them.
Diet: lanternfish and squid.
Fun fact: a chick wears a brown down coat for about a year.
Tell me about the African elephant.

Habitat: savannas and forests south of the Sahara.
Diet: grasses, leaves, bark and fruit.
Fun fact: its trunk has tens of thousands of muscles and no bones.
Tell me about the honey bee.

Habitat: hives in tree hollows and beekeepers' boxes, on every continent but Antarctica.
Diet: nectar and pollen.
Fun fact: a forager tells its hive where the flowers are with a waggle dance.
You are a field guide. Answer with a three-line card.
Tell me about the green sea turtle.

Habitat: warm coastal waters and seagrass beds.
Diet: mostly seagrass and algae, once grown.
Fun fact: a female returns to nest on the beach where she hatched.
Tell me about the snow leopard.

Habitat: the high mountains of Central Asia.
Diet: wild sheep and goats, marmots and hares.
Fun fact: it wraps its long, thick tail around itself for warmth.
Tell me about the giant panda.

Habitat: mountain bamboo forests of central China.
Diet: almost entirely bamboo.
Fun fact: it spends more than ten hours a day eating.
Tell me about the monarch butterfly.

Habitat: meadows and fields of North America, wintering in mountain forests of Mexico.
Diet: milkweed leaves as a caterpillar, nectar as an adult.
Fun fact: one generation flies south for winter, and several share the way back.
You are a field guide. Answer with a three-line card.
Tell me about the common octopus.

Habitat: rocky coasts and reefs of temperate and tropical seas.
Diet: crabs, clams and small fish.
Fun fact: it has three hearts and blue blood.
Tell me about the bald eagle.

Habitat: lakes, rivers and coasts of North America.
Diet: mostly fish, with waterfowl and carrion.
Fun fact: a pair reuses and enlarges its nest for years, into one of the largest of any bird.
Tell me about the red kangaroo.

Habitat: the dry plains of inland Australia.
Diet: grasses and shrubs.
Fun fact: it uses its tail as a fifth leg when it walks slowly.
Tell me about the Arctic tern.

Habitat: Arctic coasts in the northern summer, Antarctic seas in the southern.
Diet: small fish and crustaceans.
Fun fact: it flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year.
You are a field guide. Answer with a three-line card.
Tell me about the giraffe.

Habitat: savannas and open woodlands of Africa.
Diet: leaves, most of all acacia.
Fun fact: its neck has seven vertebrae, as a human's does.
Tell me about the bottlenose dolphin.

Habitat: warm and temperate seas, along coasts and in open water.
Diet: fish and squid.
Fun fact: each one has a signature whistle that works as its name.
Tell me about the platypus.

Habitat: rivers and streams of eastern Australia.
Diet: insect larvae, shrimp and worms from the riverbed.
Fun fact: it finds prey with electric sensors in its bill, its eyes closed.
Tell me about the chameleon.

Habitat: forests of Madagascar and Africa.
Diet: insects.
Fun fact: its eyes move independently, so it can look two ways at once.
